drug_class: CGRP (calcitonin gene-related peptide) antagonist / monoclonal antibody
purpose: Eptinezumab-jjmr is used to prevent migraines in adults. It helps reduce how often you get migraines before they even start. This medicine is for people who get migraines frequently and need ongoing prevention.
how_it_works: Your body makes a protein called CGRP, which plays a big role in triggering migraines. This medication is a specially designed antibody that blocks that protein so it cannot cause a migraine. By blocking CGRP, it helps keep migraines from happening in the first place.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include stuffy or runny nose, sore throat, and feeling tired. Some people may also have a reaction at the infusion site or feel flushed during the IV infusion. These side effects are usually mild and go away on their own.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have ever had a serious allergic reaction to any medication, since allergic reactions including serious ones can occur with this drug. Let your healthcare team know all other medications you take before starting. This medicine is given by IV infusion in a clinic, so you should not try to give it to yourself at home. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding.
typical_dosing: This medication is given as an IV infusion (through a vein) by a healthcare professional in a clinic or infusion center. The usual dose is 100 mg given once every 3 months, though some patients may receive 300 mg every 3 months based on their doctor's recommendation. Each infusion takes about 30 minutes.
